subject: fix(context): P10.8 — a compaction has to be worth its round trip
prompt:
Context compaction (`ContextEngine.compactWorkingSet` in packages/orchestrator/src/context-engine.ts) can pay for a summarizer round trip and free almost nothing. The verbatim tail is sized in TOKENS against the real context window but floored by a MESSAGE COUNT (`recentK`), and the count defeats the budget:

1. Six recent tool-heavy messages can be larger than the whole tail budget. Honouring `recentK` there kept 32,649 of 33,046 tokens verbatim: compaction "succeeded", summarized eleven small messages, freed 1.2%, and left the trigger hot for the next turn. (A parallel batch of reads arrives as one assistant message plus one tool message; when the budget lands between two such batches, snapping the cut backward to a pair-safe boundary walks past both and the budget is lost again.)
2. A head that is a sliver of the working set is summarized anyway: 13 small messages of 387 tokens in front of a 20,938-token working set were folded, for the price of a round trip.
3. A summary can be no smaller than what it replaces: an explicit compaction measured 16,929 → 16,931 tokens and was applied, losing the verbatim text as well.
4. An explicit or forced compaction cuts to the conservative 30% tail, so against a tail budget larger than the whole conversation it can only nibble the oldest few messages (141 tokens of a 5,027-token set) — not what "free up context now" asks for.

What should happen:
- The count floor yields when honouring it would keep a tail well past the token budget (some overrun is fine — a tail of one message is not a conversation — but not several times the budget), and a pair-safe cut must not give the budget back by walking past large batches. In case 1 compaction must free a meaningful share of the working set.
- A head that is a small fraction of the working set (under roughly 15%) is not summarized: the free tier (evicting old tool-result bodies) may still run, and otherwise the result is an honest no-op, with no summarizer call.
- A summary that would not make the working set smaller is discarded: the transcript is returned unchanged, not compacted, marked as a no-op with a reason saying the summary is "no smaller" than what it would replace.
- A forced compaction (the `force` option: the provider rejected the request as too large) and a requested one (`requestCompaction()`, behind the `compact_context` tool) keep only the recent exchange — the last `recentK` messages — and fold the rest into the summary. The automatic policy keeps its 30% tail.
- The result says what asked for the compaction, and the loop surfaces a no-op as a notice rather than doing nothing silently. The compaction event may carry the tier and trigger as well (it is defined in packages/protocol/src/events.ts).

Keep the existing exported APIs working, and keep the existing tests passing.

Interface the fix must provide — on the object `compactWorkingSet` resolves to:
- `noop?: boolean` and `noopReason?: string` — the compaction was considered and deliberately not applied.
- `trigger?: "auto" | "requested" | "overflow"` — "auto" for the automatic high-water compaction, "requested" when `requestCompaction()` asked for it, "overflow" when the caller passed `force: true`. Present on every result that compacted.
